verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              कृतविद्ये कचे प्राप्ते हृष्टरूपा दिवौकसः। कचादधीत्य तां विद्यां कृतार्था भरतर्षभ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: O best of the Bharata race, the dwellers of heaven were exceedingly glad to get back Kacha who had learnt the knowledge (of Sanjivini). The celestial then learnt the Sanjivini from Kacha and considered their object achieved.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रणशिता प्रणंक्ष्यति । भागभाक् भागः अयमेव कचो वेदे ‘शंयु’ शब्देनोच्यते । यदेवाब्रह्मणोक्तो श्रद्दधानो यजते शंयुमेव तस्य बार्हस्पत्यं यज्ञस्याशीर्गच्छति एतन्मे मेत्यब्रवीत्किं मे प्रजाया इति योपगुरातैशतेन यातयाद्योनिहनत्सहस्त्रेण यातयाद्यो लोहितं करवद्यावतः प्रस्कन्द्य पांसून्संगृह्णात्तावतः संवत्सरान्पितृलोकं न प्राजानादिति । तस्माद्ब्राह्मणाय नापगुरेत न निहन्यान्न लोहितं कुर्यादिति श्रुतो वरस्तद्भाक् । अपगुरेत न गालयेत् । शतादयो नरकविशेषाः  ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्व एव समागम्य शतक्रतुमथाब्रुवन्। कालस्ते विक्रमस्याद्य जहि शत्रून्पुरन्दर॥२॥
verses.english: They all assembled together and thus spoke to Indra. “O Indra, the time has come to show your prowess. Kill your enemies."
verses.bhavadeepa: अष्टसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः कृतविद्य इति ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु सहितैस्त्रिदशैर्मघवांस्तदा। तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रचक्राम सोऽपश्यत वने स्त्रियः॥३॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed, Indra said “Be it so." He then, accompanied by the celestials set out. He saw many damsels in the forest.

verses.sanskrit: क्रीडन्तीनां तु कन्यानां वने चैत्ररथोपमे। वायुभूतः स वस्त्राणि सर्वाण्येव व्यमिश्रयत्॥४॥
verses.english: The maidens were sporting in a lake in the wood which was like that of Chitraratha. Changing himself into wind, he (Indra) mixed up their clothes.
verses.bhavadeepa: मघवान् इन्द्रः । ‘मखेषु मघवानसौ’ इति भट्टिः । प्रचक्राम भूतलं प्रतीति शेषः॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो जलात्समुत्तीर्य कन्यास्ताः सहितास्तदा। वस्त्राणि जगृहुस्तानि यथा सन्नान्यनेकशः॥५॥
verses.english: The maidens, after rising from the water all together, put on the clothes which each got near her from the mixed up heap. The cloth of Devayani was thus taken up and worn by Sharmishtha, the daughter of king Vrishaparva, not knowing that it belonged to others.
verses.bhavadeepa: वायुभूत इन्द्रः । कन्याद्वयद्वारा शुक्रदानवयोर्विरोधोत्पादनार्थम् ॥ ४॥

verses.sanskrit: तत्र वासो देवयानयाः शर्मिष्ठा जगृहे तदा। व्यतिमिश्रमजानन्ती दुहिता वृषपर्वणः॥६॥
ततस्तयोर्मिथस्तत्र विरोधः समजायत। देवयान्याश्च राजेन्द्र शर्मिष्ठायाश्च तत्कृते॥७॥
verses.english: O great king, a dispute, thereupon, arose between Devayani and Sharmishtha.

verses.sanskrit:
देवयान्युवाच।
              कस्माद्गृह्णासि मे वस्त्रं शिष्या भूत्वा ममासुरि। समुदाचारहीनाया न ते साधु भविष्यति॥८॥
verses.english: Devayani said : O daughter of the Asura, how do you dare take my cloth, being my pupil. Destitute of good conduct, nothing good can come to you.

verses.sanskrit:
शर्मिष्ठोवाच।
              आसीनं च शयानं च पिता ते पितरं मम। स्तौति बन्दीव चाभीक्ष्णं नीचैः स्थित्वा विनीतवत्॥९॥
verses.english: Sharmishtha said : Whether my father is sitting or lying your father, occupying a lower seat and casting his eyes downwards, adores him like a Vandi (a chanter of praises.)
verses.bhavadeepa: समुदाचरः सदाचारः  ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: याचतस्त्वं हि दुहिता स्तुवतः प्रतिगृह्णतः। सुताहं स्तूयमानस्य ददतोऽप्रतिगृह्णतः॥१०॥
verses.english: You are the daughter of a man who begs and I am the daughter of one who bestows alms. your father chants praises of others and my father's praises are chanted. Your father lives on alms, my father bestows them. O beggar's girl, you are free to strike your breast, to use harsh words, to vow enmity to me and to give way to your wrath. O beggarly woman, you weep in vain. You cannot harm me, though I can harm you. You desire to quarrel with me, but I do not at all consider you as my equal.

verses.sanskrit:
आदुन्वस्व विदुन्वस्व द्रुह्य कुप्यस्व याचकि। अनायुधा सायुधाया रिक्ता क्षुभ्यसि भिक्षुकि।	
              लप्स्यसे प्रतियोद्धारं न हि त्वां गणयाम्यहम्॥११॥

वैशंपायन उवाच।
              समुच्छ्रयं देवयानीं गतां सक्तां च वाससि॥१२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this, Devayani became very angry and she began to tear her cloth. But Sharmishtha, throwing her into a well, went away to her home. The wicked Sharmishtha thought her to be dead and went home in a wrathful mood. When she went away, the son of Nahusha, Yayati came to that place; he was after deer.
verses.bhavadeepa: आदुन्वस्वेति । ‘अत्र यथा इन्द्रेण युजातरुषेमवृत्रमित्यत्र उः सिप्शप् चेतिबहुलं छंदसीति बाहुलकाद्विकरणत्रयम् । एवमिहाप्यार्षत्वात् श्नुः शप् चेतिविकरणद्वयम् । आदुन्वस्व आभिमुख्येन वक्षस्ताडनादिना संतांपं प्राप्नुहि । विदुन्वस्व पांसुषु लुंठनादिना । द्रुह्य द्रोहं चिरकालिकं क्रोधं कुरु । कुप्यस्व सद्यः परानिष्टफलो यत्नः कोपस्तं कुरु । रिक्ता दरिद्रा  ॥११॥

verses.sanskrit: शर्मिष्ठा प्राक्षिपत्कूपे ततः स्वपुरमागमत्। हतेयमिति विज्ञाय शर्मिष्ठा पापनिश्चया॥१३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रतियोद्धारं प्रहर्तारं शत्रुं मामेव । समुच्छ्रयं सत्यवचनेन महत्त्वम्  ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: अनवेक्ष्य ययौ वेश्म क्रोधवेगपरायणा। अथ तं देशमभ्यागाद्ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः॥१४॥
श्रान्तयुग्मः श्रान्तहयो मृगलिप्सुः पिपासितः। स नाहुषः प्रेक्षमाण उदपानं गतोदकम्॥१५॥
verses.english: The pair of horses in his car were fatigued and he himself was thirsty. That son of Nahusha (Yayati) saw a well in which there was no water.

verses.sanskrit: ददर्श राजा तां तत्र कन्यामग्निशिखामिव। तामपृच्छत्स दृष्ट्वैव कन्याममरवर्णिनीम्॥१६॥
verses.english: There (in that well) the king saw a maiden as effulgent as fire. Seeing her within the well, the illustrious king addressed that girl who was as beautiful as a celestial maiden.
verses.bhavadeepa: युग्याः रथवाहकाः । हयाः केवलाश्वाः । उदकं पीयतेऽस्मादिति उदपानं कूपम्॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: सान्त्वयित्वा नृपश्रेष्ठः साम्ना परमवल्गुना। का त्वं ताम्रनखी श्यामा सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डला॥१७॥
verses.english: Thai best of kings, pacifying her with sweet words said, O fair lady, O lady with bright nails, as burnished copper and with earrings of celestial gems, who are you?

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घं ध्यायसि चात्यर्थं कस्माच्छिचषि चातुरा। कथं च पतिताऽस्यस्मिन्कूपे वीरुत्तृणावृते॥१८॥
verses.english: Why are you in such anxiety? Why are you weeping in distress? How have you fallen into this well covered with long grass and creepers? O beauty of slender-waist, tell me truly, whose daughter are you?
verses.bhavadeepa: वल्गुना मञ्जुना। श्यामा षोडशवार्षिकी यौवनारुढा। सुमृष्ठानि दिव्यानि॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit:
दुहिता चैव कस्य त्वं वद सत्यं सुमध्यमे।
              देवयान्युवाच।
              योऽसौ देवैर्हतान्दैत्यानुत्थापयति विद्यया॥१९॥
तस्य शुक्रस्य कन्याहं स मां नूनं न बुध्यते। एष मे दक्षिणो राजन्पाणिस्ताम्रनखाङ्गुलिः॥२०॥
verses.english: Devayani said : I am the daughter of Shukra who revives the Asuras, killed by the celestial. He knows not what has befallen me.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्धर गृहीत्वा मां कुलीनस्त्वं हि मे मतः। जानामि हि त्वां संशान्तं वीर्यवन्तं यशस्विनम्॥२१॥
verses.english: O king, this is my right hand with nails as bright as the burnished copper. You are nobly born, I ask you, take my hand and raise me up. I know, you are very gentle, very powerful and greatly famous. You should raise me up from this well.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्मां पतितामस्मात्कूपादुद्धर्तुमर्हसि।
              वैशंपायन उवाच।
              तामथो ब्राह्मणीं कन्यां विज्ञाय नहुषात्मजः॥२२॥
गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे पाणावुज्जहार ततोऽवटात्। उद्धृत्य चैनां तरसा तस्मात्कूपान्नराधिपः॥२३॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : The son of Nahusha, king (Yayati) having learnt that she was the daughter of a Brahmana, took hold of her right hand and raised her up from that well. The king, after speedily raising her from the well and speaking sweet and courteous words to that beauty of tapering thighs, went away to his own capital. After the departure of the son of Nahusha (Yayati), the faultless featured Devayani spoke in sorrow to Ghurnika who came there.

verses.sanskrit: आमन्त्रयित्वा सुश्रेणीं ययातिः स्वपुरं ययौ। गते तु नाहुषे तस्मिन्देवयन्यप्यनिन्दिता॥२४॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अवटात् गर्तात्  ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit:
उवाच शोकसंतप्ता घूर्णिकामागतां पुरः।
              देवयान्युवाच।
              त्वरितं घूर्णिके गच्छ शीघ्रमाचक्ष्व मे पितुः॥२५॥

नेदानीं संप्रवेक्ष्यामि नगरं वृषपर्वणः।
              वैशंपायन उवाच।
              सा तत्र त्वरितं गत्वा घूर्णिकाऽसुरमन्दिरम्॥२६॥
verses.english: Devayani said : O Ghurnika, go speedily to my father and tell him as soon as possible all that had happened. I shall not enter the city of Vrishaparva.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा काव्यमुवाचेदं संभ्रमाविष्टचेतना। आचचक्षे महाप्राज्ञं देवयानीं वने हताम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: Ghurnika speedily went to the palace of the Asura (chief). Finding the son of Kavi (Shukra), she spoke to his thus, her perception having been dimmed by anger. “O great Brahmana, O illustrious man, I tell you, Devayani had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva. Having heard that his daughter had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, he soon went to search for her with a heavy heart. And when he found her in the forest, the son of Kavi embraced her with affection and spoke to her with his voice choked with grief. “The weal and woe that befall on people is always due to their own faults. You had some fault, I am sure, which has been thus expiated."

verses.sanskrit: शर्मिष्ठया महाभाग दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः। श्रुत्वा दुहितरं काव्यस्तत्र शर्मिष्ठया हताम्॥२८॥
verses.bhavadeepa: हताम् ताडिताम्  ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: त्वरया निर्ययौ दुःखान्मार्गमाणः सुतां वने। दृष्ट्वा दुहितरं काव्यो देवयानीं ततो वने॥२९॥
बाहुभ्यां संपरिष्वज्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। आत्मदोषैर्नियच्छन्ती सर्वे दुःखसुखे जनाः॥३०॥

मन्ये दुश्चरितं तेऽस्ति यस्येयं निष्कृतिः कृता।
              देवयान्युवाच।
              निष्कृतिर्मेऽस्तु वा मास्तु शृणुष्वावहितो मम॥३१॥
verses.bhavadeepa: नियच्छन्ति प्रयच्छन्ति । आत्मदोषैर्हेतुभिः स्वकर्मभिरेव सुखदुःखे जनात्प्राप्येते न तु जनस्यापराध इत्यर्थः  ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: शर्मिष्ठया यदुक्ताऽस्मि दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः। सत्यं किलैतत्सा प्राह दैत्यानामसि गायनः॥३२॥
verses.english: Devayani said: Be it punishment of my fault or not (O father), hear all that the daughter of Vrishaparva, Sharmishtha, had said to me. She has said, (I say) truly, that you are a Bandi (hired chanter) of the Asura king. Even thus did Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, speak. These cruel and piercing words, with her eyes red (with anger). (She said), “You are the daughter of one who always chants the praise of others for hire and who always asks for charity.
verses.bhavadeepa: एतदेवाह । मन्ये इति । निष्कृतिः फलभोगेन निरसनम्  ॥३१॥

verses.sanskrit: एवं हि मे कथयति शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी। वचनं तीक्ष्णपरुषं क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा भृशम्॥३३॥
स्तुवतो दुहिता नित्यं याचतः प्रतिगृह्णतः। अहं तु स्तूयमानस्य ददतोऽप्रतिगृह्णतः॥३४॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तीक्ष्णं मर्मभित् । यतः परुषं निष्ठुराक्षरम् ।  ॥३३॥

verses.sanskrit: इदं मामाह शर्मिष्ठा दुहिता वृषपर्वणः। क्रोधसंरक्तनयना दर्पपूर्णा पुनः पुनः॥३५॥
verses.english: And who accepts alms, whereas I am the daughter of one who is the adored of all, who gives alms and never receives and gift from any body.” Thus again and again spoke to me Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, full of pride, her eyes red in anger.

verses.sanskrit: यद्यहं स्तुवतस्तात दुहिता प्रतिगृह्णतः। प्रसादयिष्ये शर्मिष्ठामित्युक्ता तु सखी मया॥३६॥
verses.english: O father, if I am really the daughter of a hired chanter of others' praises and of one who accepts alms, I must adore her in the hope of getting her favour. I have already told this to her.
verses.bhavadeepa: इदं पूर्वोक्तम्  ॥३५॥

verses.sanskrit:
शुक्र उवाच।
              स्तुवतो दुहिता न त्वं याचतः प्रतिगृह्णतः। अस्तोतुः स्तूयमानस्य दुहिता देवयान्यसि॥३७॥
verses.english: Shukra said: O Devayani, you are not the daughter of a hired chanter of praises, nor that of one who asks for alms and receives them. You are the daughter of one who is adored by all and who adores none.

verses.sanskrit: वृषपर्वैव तद्वेद शक्रो राजा च नाहुषः। अचिन्त्यं ब्रह्म निर्द्वन्द्वमैश्वरं हि बलं मम॥३८॥
verses.english: Vrishaparva and Indra and king Yayati, (all) know my strength to be inconceivable like Brahma and unapproachable God.

verses.sanskrit: यच्च किंचित्सर्वगतं भूमौ वा यदि वा दिवि। तस्याहमीश्वरो नित्यं तुष्टेनोक्तः स्वयंभुवा॥३९॥
verses.english: The Self created (Brahma) himself, being pleased with me said that I was the lord of that which was in all things on earth or in heaven.
verses.bhavadeepa: नाहुषो ययातिः । मम ऐश्वरं निर्द्वंद्वमप्रतिपक्षं बलमस्ति  ॥३८॥

verses.sanskrit: अहं जलं विमुञ्चामि प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। पुष्णाम्यौषधयः सर्वा इति सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥४०॥
verses.english: I tell you truly, that it is I who pour rain for the good of all and nourish the annual plants that sustain all living creatures.
verses.bhavadeepa: ईश्वरत्वमेवाह । यच्चेति । स्वयंभुवा तत्त्वमसीत्यादिना वेदेन करणेन तुष्टेन गुरुणेति शेषः  ॥३९॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              एवं विषादमापन्नां मन्युना संप्रपीडिताम्। वचनैर्मधुरैः श्लक्ष्णैः सान्त्वयामास तां पिता॥४१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : It was thus with such sweet and sensible words, the father tried to pacify his angry and sorrowful daughter.
verses.bhavadeepa: अहं मनुरभवं यत्सूर्यश्चेति वदन्वामदेव इव स्वस्य सार्वात्म्यानुभवमाह । अहमिति॥४०॥
